mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 0.25%, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.25% signals an ultra-loose monetary policy that stimulates economic activity and equity returns, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 0.25%, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals strong consumer demand and economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS rise by more than 0.5% MoM, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In high unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 5.0%), weak consumer spending and corporate earnings lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0%, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is above -0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates a robust labor market, supporting consumer spending and corporate earnings, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for PAYEMS as a predictor of 20-day SPX returns is negative over any 3-year rolling window, or the average 20-day return when PAYEMS is above 145,000 (thousands) is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 1,650,000 units, it signals strong economic activity and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when HOUST > 1650.0, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year CPI increase above 3.0% signals persistent inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which compresses equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.0%, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is above -0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A higher industrial production (INDPRO) level signals robust manufacturing activity and economic growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for INDPRO as a predictor of 5-day SPX returns is negative over any 3-year rolling window, or the average 5-day return when INDPRO is above 100.0 is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).
